general_comment:
[maas-code-reviewer review]

> LLM-generated review from https://github.com/canonical/maas-code-reviewer.
> Intended to assist a human reviewer, not replace one — suggestions may be
> incorrect, please verify before acting.


Scope mismatch first: the description says this change (1) switches to the canonical `LP: #<id>` format, (2) adds a format check, and (3) writes a comment on the LP bug with the PR/commit link. The full diff contains only one new step in `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` — item (2). `.github/workflows/lp-bug-update.yaml`, `utilities/mark_lp_bug_fix_committed.py`, and `AGENTS.md` (which documents `Resolves LP:2066936` at lines 99/131/154) are untouched. Either the diff is incomplete or the description is stale; please reconcile.

Functional blocker: the new check enforces `LP:<digits>`, i.e. it **rejects** `Fixes LP: #2066936`. Per the Launchpad comment-syntax reference you cite (https://ubuntu.com/docs/launchpad/user/reference/comment-syntax/#mention-multiple-launchpad-bugs), `LP: #<num>` is the linking pattern and `LP #1` (no colon) is *not* linked. So as written the workflow fails PRs that use exactly the format the commit message claims to standardize on. If the goal is `LP: #<id>`, the regex must accept (and require) `#`, and `lp-bug-update.yaml`'s extraction regex plus the AGENTS.md examples must change in the same commit, otherwise bug auto-closing breaks for every PR written in the new format.

Detection logic is also weaker than intended: the gate `keyword.*LP:\s*` only fires when `LP:` is already present, so the exact legacy spellings this is meant to catch (`Fixes LP#2066936`, `Fixes LP 2066936`, `Fixes bug 2066936`) pass silently and then go unnoticed by `lp-bug-update.yaml`. Conversely it produces false failures on `LP` without a word boundary (`...see HELP: section`) and on branch URIs (`fixed in lp:maas/+git/...`).

Finally, this validates `github.event.pull_request.body`, while `lp-bug-update.yaml` extracts from `.commits[].message` on push. That only lines up if the repo squash-merges with the PR body in the commit message; with merge-commit or rebase strategies a green check here still yields no bug update. Worth a comment stating the assumption, or move the check to the commit messages of the PR.

Good: the body is passed through `env:` rather than interpolated into the shell, avoiding the usual `${{ }}` injection/quoting hazard; workflow `permissions` stay read-only.

One trigger note outside the diff: `on.pull_request.types` (ci.yaml line 5) is `[opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]` — no `edited`. A contributor who fixes the description after this check fails gets no re-run until they push. Adding `edited` (or splitting description checks into a small dedicated workflow) would make the gate usable.

.github/workflows/ci.yaml.166: This step validates the PR description, but the consumer (`lp-bug-update.yaml`) parses `.commits[].message` on push to master. The two only agree under squash-merge-with-PR-body; under merge/rebase a passing check here still leaves the bug un-updated. State the assumption in a comment, or validate the PR's commit messages instead.
.github/workflows/ci.yaml.170: The keyword alternation is now duplicated twice in this step and a third time in `lp-bug-update.yaml`; a comment saying "keep these in sync" is the symptom. Hoist it into a shell variable here (`KEYWORDS='\b(?:close[sd]?|fix(?:e[sd])?|resolve[sd]?)\b'`) and use it in both greps; keeping the cross-workflow copy in sync still needs a deliberate update in this same commit.
.github/workflows/ci.yaml.171: Detection gate is too narrow and too loose at once. Too narrow: it requires `LP:` to already be present, so the legacy spellings this change targets (`Fixes LP#2066936`, `Fixes LP 2066936`, `Fixes bug 2066936`) skip the check entirely and then silently fail extraction in `lp-bug-update.yaml`. Too loose: there is no word boundary before `LP`, so `Fixes ... see HELP: ...` trips it, and case-insensitive `lp:` also matches Launchpad branch URIs (`fixed in lp:maas/+git/maas`), both producing spurious failures. Also note grep is line-based and `.` doesn't cross newlines, so `Fixes the parser.\n\nLP: #123` matches nothing and is skipped. Suggest `"${KEYWORDS}.*\bLP\b"` for detection and requiring the full canonical form in the validation step.
.github/workflows/ci.yaml.172: This is the blocker: `LP:\s*\K[0-9]+` requires digits immediately after the colon, so the canonical `Fixes LP: #2066936` — the format this commit says it is standardizing on, and the only one Launchpad actually links (`LP #1` is not linked per the comment-syntax reference) — fails CI. Make it `LP\s*:\s*#[0-9]+` and update `lp-bug-update.yaml`'s extraction regex (`LP:\s*\K[0-9]+`) plus the AGENTS.md examples in the same commit, otherwise the two workflows disagree on the accepted format. Minor: `\K` has no effect under `-q` since nothing is printed.
.github/workflows/ci.yaml.174: Message contradicts both the PR description and the Launchpad docs, and gives no example. Once the regex accepts `#`, make this: `Expected "<keyword> LP: #<number>", e.g. "Resolves LP: #2066936".` Echoing the offending line would also help contributors.
